General Gainz Rest Time Matrix (RM vs. VDS)

In Cody Lefever’s General Gainz (2026, pp. 25, 29, 33, 35–36), rest intervals are governed by Tier and the contrast between your high-effort Top RM Set and submaximal Volume Drop Sets (VDS). Rest itself is a progression variable—gradually shortening rest drives work capacity and density. Click ▶ to launch any interval.

Tier RM & VDS Structure After Top RM Set Between VDS / MRS Effort Gap & Density Cue
T1 Primary 1–6RM + Singles (RM to RM+3)
4–6RM overlaps T2 bridge (1s or ½ RM)
Book: 3:00 – 5:00
Book: 2:00 – 3:00 (1–2m density)
Aim for 2–3 min between singles for explosive CAT bar speed; tighten to 1–2 min only as work capacity improves.
T2 Secondary 4–10RM + 3–6 VDS (½ or ¾ RM)
Quarter-Sets (¼ RM): 8–12 sets @ 30–60s
Book: 2:00 – 3:00
Book: 1:00 – 2:00 (30–60s ¼ RM)
Odd RMs round half-sets up on Easy/Moderate and down on Hard. Start ¾ RM at 3 sets; increase rest as load nears T1.
T3 Accessories 10RM+ · 3–4 Max Rep Sets (1–2 on Hard)
Ranges 15–20 → 8–10 (or 30/45/60 total)
Book: 0:30 – 1:30
Book: 0:30 – 1:30
30–90 seconds between MRS builds hypertrophy and metabolic density. T3 often runs intensification (+kg, lower rep range) even during T1/T2 accumulation.
⚡ Effort-Aware Auto-Rest & The Effort Gap
When Auto-Rest: ON is active in the top bar, checking off a Top RM launches the RM rest countdown (T1: 3–5 min, T2: 2–3 min), while checking off a VDS chip launches the VDS countdown (T1: 2–3 min, T2: 1–2 min, T3: 45–90s)—scaling cleanly across Easy / Moderate / Hard.
🗺️ Accumulation vs. Intensification in GG
Accumulation holds load steady while climbing reps & sets via Push and Extend (moving weights from T1 → T2 → T3). Intensification adds load via Find while holding volume and stepping down the RM/VDS ladder (moving weights from T3 → T2 → T1).

Book Footnotes (p. 35): Follow-up reps are flexible—not all VDS have to match (e.g., after a 7RM the first few sets may be 4s and the last few 3s). Always lift within your Technical Limit; do not push all RM sets to max effort. If the RM is skipped, apply Effort ratings to the first and last set of VDS.

The 4 Actions (Book pp. 17–18)

  • Find: Increase weight on the RM or on the VDS first (if the RM effort was too high to add load yet). Earned from performance—no percentage calculators.
  • Hold: Keep one or more variables (weight, RM, VDS, or rest) steady while improving another variable or building Quality (turning Hard → Moderate/Easy).
  • Push: Add reps per set (RM +1 rep or VDS 1s → ½ RM → ¾ RM) at the same weight, and/or shorten rest periods to raise density.
  • Extend: Add VDS sets at the same weight (T1 up to RM + 3 singles; T2 up to 6 sets), or extend rest to protect rep quality when fatigued.

Effort Guide (Book pp. 35, 55)

  • Easy (E) — 2+ RiR: Crisp, fast reps within Technical Limit. Wide effort gap—prime to Push RM/VDS, Extend sets, shorten rest, or Find +kg.
  • Moderate (M) — 1 RiR: Productive working effort with clean bar path. Ideal to Extend VDS toward cap or steadily Push RM reps.
  • Hard (H) — 0 RiR: Zero technical reps left in the tank. Trim VDS (or use 1–2 sets on T3) and Hold next session to build Quality.
  • When skipping the RM set (VDS-only), rate the first and last set (e.g., Easy → Moderate).

The 4 Vectors of Progression

  • Intensity: Heavier kg on the bar or higher validated e1RM relative to 1RM.
  • Volume: More total reps, sets, tonnage, and effective 16-muscle sets per week.
  • Density: More work per minute (higher kg/min) via shorter rest or faster concentric speed.
  • Quality: Repeating the same weight & reps with better posture, bar speed, and lower Effort rating.

⚡ CAT — Compensatory Acceleration

Popularized by Dr. Fred Hatfield and central to GG (pp. 15–16): intentionally accelerate every VDS rep as explosively as possible through the concentric—especially as leverage improves near lockout.

Put heavy-weight intent into submaximal singles and half-sets. Moving a weight faster than last week is getting stronger, building maximal force production without max-load fatigue.

🛡️ Technical Limit & The Injury Gap

Technical Limit is the most weight/reps you can lift with consistent posture and control. Limit Strength is your absolute max with form breakdown (pp. 22, 57).

The gap between them is your Injury Gap. Rate effort against your Technical Limit—if form breaks down, it was a Hard set regardless of reps left. Crisp VDS reps close the gap safely.

🎯 The Effort Gap & RM Variations

The Effort Gap is RM − VDS reps (pp. 55–56). A wider gap (e.g., 5RM → singles = 4-rep gap) keeps VDS fast for skill & CAT; closing the gap (¾-sets, pauses, shorter rest) drives endurance & size.

Book RM Variations (pp. 48–54): Skip RM (VDS-only grease the groove / deload), Skip VDS (RM-only peak / recovery), Last Set RM (VDS first → final RM), and Bookend RM (RM1 + 2–3 VDS + RM2 calibration).

🌿 Three Pillars of Recovery & Rest Days (pp. 66–68)

Training creates the stimulus—recovery creates the gainz. Before dropping weights or changing splits during a rough patch, audit the three pillars:

  • 1. Nutrition & Hydration: Adequate total calories, protein, carbs around lifting, and electrolytes/water to fuel work density.
  • 2. Sleep (7–8+ Hours): Consistent sleep window is the #1 force multiplier for nervous system readiness and bar speed.
  • 3. Stress & Active Recovery (GPP): Manage life stress and use rest days for low-impact blood flow (walking, mobility, light conditioning)—not extra Hard RMs.

🧭 Effort Calibration & Feedback Loop (pp. 11–12, 55–56)

General Gainz runs on a continuous Action → Effort Data → Trend → Adjustment feedback loop. Use your VDS performance to self-calibrate RM ratings:

  • Hard RM + Crisp Extended VDS: You likely overrated RM difficulty—re-rate it Moderate (p. 55) rather than capping progress prematurely.
  • Easy/Mod RM + Subpar VDS: You underrated fatigue or rest was too tight—extend rest, widen the Effort Gap (¾ → ½ RM or Mix taper), or drop T2 load (p. 28).
  • Multi-Session Stalls / Quality Dips: 2+ consecutive Hard or Subpar sessions signal time to Hold, run a Skip RM deload (p. 52), and check your Recovery Pillars.
